newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PDVSA SAYS FORCE MAJEURE ON NINE GASOLINE CARGOES.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA SAYS FORCE MAJEURE ON NINE GASOLINE CARGOES.

text.p: Venezuela's state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) declared force majeure on a total of nine August loadings of gasoline after fires at the Curacao and Cardon refineries cut output, a company spokeswoman said on Thursday.

Of the nine cargoes, two have been cancelled and three loadings of 230,000 barrels each remain to be resolved, said the spokeswoman for PDVSA subsidiary Maraven, which manages the two refineries. Three clients agreed to accept gasoline components instead of their contractual supplies, and one client was supplied from an outside purchase.
Three of the nine cargoes were 10,000-40,000 barrel cargoes, the spokeswoman added.
Contractual sales of other products, such as diesel, fuel oil and jet fuel, would be fulfilled and she did not expect Maraven to make any more cargo cancellations.

The problems in Cardon originated from a fire in a hydro- desulphurization unit on July 28 which contaminated the reformer, a gasoline producing unit. Trading sources said the 60,000 barrel per day (bpd) reformer was running below capacity and was not producing high octane gasoline.

In Curacao, a major fire last Thursday disabled the main crude distillation unit, cutting refinery throughput by 130,000 bpd to 60,000 bpd. By Friday, crude runs rose to 105,000 bpd and a senior refinery source expected to return to 170,000 bpd on August 22.
Both refineries are major exporters of gasoline and other refined products to the U.S. market.
